newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major unveils "Basic Pension Plus".
newsitem.headline: UK's Major unveils "Basic Pension Plus".

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major said on Tuesday that his government will introduce a new pension scheme for future generations.
But he pledged that the entitlement of the current working generation to the basic pension and to SERPS (the State Earnings Related Pensions Scheme) will remain the same.
"My intention is to ensure that all of the younger generation can look forward to the benefits and security of a pension fund built up in their own name," Major told a press conference.
He said the new scheme was called "Basic Pension Plus."
"Every young person will be able to accumulate an investment fund which will yield considerably more than the basic state pension," he said.
"We propose the younger generation will have part of their national insurance contributions paid into a pension fund...that they choose to invest the money on their behalf."
He said in the future, assuming reasonable investment growth and even on a minimum contribution, retiring people should receive considerably more than the current state pension.
